topic: Exact Euclidean rank-preservation and sharp rank-margin inference for multivariate Brenier counterfactual mechanisms; use the full queued specification and unverified presolve draft at <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_brenier_crossregime_rank_margin_frontier.md

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when smooth regime-specific Brenier mechanisms sharing a latent vector rank induce a cross-regime counterfactual map that is Euclidean monotone, strongly monotone, or cyclically monotone.

source_refs.claim: The paper distinguishes multivariate matching notions and states that a precise characterization of SCMs inducing cyclically monotone counterfactuals is unknown.
source_refs.author: Lucas De Lara and Luca Ganassali

source_refs.claim: The paper claims that monotone multivariate mechanisms produce monotone, rank-preserving counterfactual transport maps.
source_refs.author: Fabio De Sousa Ribeiro, Ainkaran Santhirasekaram, and Ben Glocker

source_refs.claim: Conditional vector quantiles are gradients of convex potentials from a common reference rank distribution.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Carlier, Victor Chernozhukov, and Alfred Galichon

open_problems.why_unsolved: De Lara and Ganassali explicitly leave the causal characterization incomplete, while Ribeiro et al. assert cross-regime monotonicity from mechanism-level monotonicity. The unresolved boundary appears at the derivative of the inverse composition: a product of positive-definite regime Hessians need not be symmetric, and its symmetric part need not be positive. The supplied presolve draft proposes a symmetric cross-Hessian criterion, commutation criterion, and Gaussian counterexample, but it is explicitly unverified and therefore constitutes a hypothesis requiring proof or refutation rather than evidence that the gap is closed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A verification or refutation of the presolve hypothesis through a necessary-and-sufficient Hessian-product characterization of Euclidean monotonicity, its sharp strong-monotonicity modulus, and cyclic monotonicity, with a valid two-dimensional noncommuting counterexample and sufficient commuting subclasses.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing separates competing multivariate notions of rank preservation before asking which causal mechanisms license each matching.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Marginals admit many deterministic matchings -> multivariate monotonicity notions diverge -> causal interpretation requires structural restrictions -> characterize the exact Euclidean cross-regime frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the common-reference vector-quantile representation and differentiate the inverse composition of two convex-gradient maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its latent-rank representation supplies exactly the regime maps whose cross-regime geometry must be characterized.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt smooth plug-in Brenier-map estimation and stability bounds to estimated inverse compositions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After the algebraic frontier is identified, these estimators provide a direct route to estimating its map-level ingredients.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp minimax separation rate and uniformly valid one-sided inference for the global cross-regime Euclidean rank margin when the margin approaches or equals zero.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves pointwise CLTs for smooth Brenier maps on a flat torus and failure of global L2 weak convergence in sufficiently high dimension.
source_refs.author: Tudor Manole, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Jonathan Niles-Weed, and Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes near-minimax L2 rates for a smooth optimal-transport map, not its Hessian or a global cross-regime eigenvalue margin.
source_refs.author: Jan-Christian Hütter and Philippe Rigollet

source_refs.claim: The paper proves global and local convergence results for empirical multivariate rank and quantile maps but does not provide rank-margin inference.
source_refs.author: Promit Ghosal and Bodhisattva Sen

source_refs.excerpt: Adaptation, multivariate outcomes, ... and uniform mixed calibration are open.
Resolve the mixed-calibration OEQ with a concrete multiplier statistic and a spectral-tail truncation rule.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature controls map loss or pointwise map values, whereas the rank margin is a derivative-level global nonsmooth functional involving two estimated maps, matrix inversion, a minimum eigenvalue, and an infimum over the reference support. Eigenvalue multiplicity and an unknown zero-margin contact set obstruct a regular delta method, while the prior scalar conditional-transport analysis explicitly leaves multivariate outcomes and uniform boundary calibration open. The presolve rate (log n/n)^(s/(2s+d)) and its fixed-support mixture lower bound remain unverified hypotheses whose legality depends on completing the multivariate PDE and testing arguments.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A proof or counterexample for the presolve rate hypothesis, comprising an explicit bias-aware margin estimator, a simultaneous honest one-sided confidence bound over a stated Hölder and convexity class, and a matching fixed-support minimax testing lower bound from the composite null margin at most zero to separated positive alternatives.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates the transition from Brenier-map estimation to inference and clearly isolates the failure of global weak convergence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Brenier maps are identifiable and estimable -> rank preservation depends on their local geometry -> pointwise map CLTs do not control a global derivative margin -> derive sharp inference for the margin itself.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt quantitative Monge–Ampère linearization to obtain stochastic expansions for the derivatives of two estimated maps and their inverse composition.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The margin is a nonlinear derivative functional of the same smooth plug-in maps, so this linearization supplies the leading stochastic term.

method_exemplars.technique: Modify the wavelet estimator and Assouad-style perturbation construction so loss is measured by the cross-regime Hessian margin.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies both smooth OT estimation machinery and a lower-bound template, while the new construction must preserve supports and change the derivative margin.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt second-order directional-delta and derivative-aware bootstrap arguments at a first-order-degenerate null.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The zero-margin boundary is nonregular, so calibration must explicitly handle degeneracy rather than invoke an ordinary Gaussian delta method.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a boundary-uniform endpoint response theorem for the second-boundary-value Monge–Ampère equation that is strong enough to deliver sharp Hessian and cross-regime rank-margin bands on compact uniformly convex supports.

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes the linear response of Brenier potentials on uniformly convex domains and proves quantitative stability, but its potential estimates do not directly yield a uniform Hessian band.
source_refs.author: F.-U. Caja-Lopez, Matias G. Delgadino, and Jun Kitagawa

source_refs.claim: The paper proves boundary regularity for conormal and oblique elliptic problems with Dini mean-oscillation data, supporting but not specializing the needed quantitative endpoint estimate.
source_refs.author: Hongjie Dong, Jihoon Lee, and Seick Kim

source_refs.claim: The available smooth-map CLT uses periodic boundary conditions on the flat torus rather than an oblique second-boundary-value problem.
source_refs.author: Tudor Manole, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Jonathan Niles-Weed, and Larry Wasserman

open_problems.why_unsolved: Periodic analysis removes the support boundary, whereas a fixed convex target produces a normalized elliptic equation with conormal or oblique boundary data and an exact mass-compatibility constraint. Existing differentiability and Dini-regularity results provide major ingredients, but they do not yet supply the tracked, boundary-uniform logarithmic endpoint estimate and quadratic nonlinear remainder needed to turn density error into sup-norm Hessian error. The first proof step is the uniform conormal half-space or boundary-parametrix cancellation; an interior Green estimate cannot control the boundary. The presolve draft states this estimate but explicitly identifies it as its unproved analytic bottleneck.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A verification or disproof of the presolve endpoint claim through a normalized global estimate of the form sup-norm Hessian response at most density sup-error times one plus its logarithm, uniform over the stated domain and coefficient class, together with a quadratic C2 remainder theorem and the resulting honest Hessian-band rate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative shows how quantitative PDE linearization becomes the decisive step in statistical inference for smooth optimal-transport maps.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Smooth plug-in maps permit pointwise inference on a torus -> causal applications use bounded Euclidean supports -> the support boundary changes the response equation -> prove boundary-uniform Hessian control for rank-margin inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Use divergence-form Monge–Ampère linearization, mean-zero normalization, and the exact conormal compatibility condition along smooth density paths.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the precise deterministic response equation that must be sharpened from potential stability to an endpoint Hessian estimate.

method_exemplars.technique: Specialize the global conormal and oblique Dini-regularity proof, tracking boundary-chart cancellation and dyadic-shell constants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired logarithmic response bound is the quantitative Dini-endpoint analogue of their boundary regularity theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer its stochastic linearization and bias decomposition, replacing periodic elliptic inversion with the verified conormal-boundary response operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how the resulting deterministic response estimate feeds into a limit theorem for a smooth plug-in Brenier estimator.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the families of multivariate regime laws whose pairwise Brenier maps form a coherent same-unit counterfactual system satisfying identity, inversion, and path independence through a common latent Euclidean rank.

source_refs.claim: Counterfactual maps obey a cocycle and path-independence algebra that pairwise cyclically monotone transports need not satisfy.
source_refs.author: Lucas De Lara and Luca Ganassali

source_refs.claim: Transport-based counterfactuals are selected couplings across observable distributions, and coincidence with causal counterfactuals requires additional assumptions.
source_refs.author: Lucas De Lara, Alberto González-Sanz, Nicholas Asher, Laurent Risser, and Jean-Michel Loubes

source_refs.excerpt: every continuous bijection ... is exactly g_v(u)=Q_v(u) ... or ... g_v(u)=Q_v(1-u)

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pairwise Brenier uniqueness is a two-marginal fact, while counterfactual coherence is a multi-regime cocycle restriction. De Lara and Ganassali exhibit path-independence failure, and the prior CausalSmith construction obtains compatibility only in the scalar case by reducing every admissible transport to a quantile or its reflection. That scalar orientation classification has no direct multivariate analogue: separately fitted convex-gradient maps need not factor through one common latent coordinate, and observational marginals alone do not reveal the residual incompatible mechanism fiber.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if representation theorem for coherent Brenier-cocycle families in terms of a common latent reference or equivalent joint potential conditions, with a constructive recovery functional under compatibility and two observationally equivalent incompatible SCMs establishing the failure frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes the tension between canonical pairwise transport and counterfactual algebra explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Each pair of marginals has a canonical Brenier map -> same-unit counterfactuals must compose across worlds -> pairwise optimal maps can violate path independence -> identify exactly when the entire Brenier family is jointly causal.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt reference-based transport factorization and the identity, inversion, and path-independence algebra to a family restricted to Brenier maps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result is the Brenier specialization of its counterfactual transport compatibility problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each regime by a convex-gradient vector quantile map from a common reference and derive compatibility conditions on the resulting potentials.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed coherent family is precisely a joint common-reference vector-quantile representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical forward and reverse multivariate rank maps to estimate common-reference factorizations and cocycle residuals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A recovered coherent family can be estimated through the empirical rank and quantile maps controlled in that paper.

literature_map:
De Lara and Ganassali (2025, arXiv:2509.16027) distinguish cyclically monotone, quantile-preserving, and triangular multivariate matchings.
They show that counterfactual maps obey a cocycle and path-independence algebra that pairwise Brenier maps need not satisfy.
Their open-questions discussion leaves a precise characterization of SCMs inducing cyclically monotone counterfactuals unresolved.
Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2510.08294) claim monotone, rank-preserving multivariate counterfactual maps through dynamic optimal transport.
Carlier, Chernozhukov, and Galichon (Annals of Statistics 2016) provide the common-reference vector-quantile representation underlying regime-specific Brenier mechanisms.
De Lara et al. (JMLR 2024) explain why a transport-selected coupling requires extra assumptions before it can be interpreted causally.
Chernozhukov et al. (Annals of Statistics 2017) and Ghosal–Sen (Annals of Statistics 2022) establish canonical multivariate ranks and empirical-map consistency, not cross-regime derivative margins.
Hütter–Rigollet (Annals of Statistics 2021) and Manole et al. (Annals of Statistics 2024) establish sharp or near-minimax smooth Brenier-map estimation rates.
Manole et al. (arXiv:2312.12407) prove pointwise smooth-map CLTs on the flat torus and show that global L2 weak convergence can fail.
The located primary literature does not convert those results into honest inference for an infimum eigenvalue of a cross-regime Jacobian.
González-Sanz and Sheng (arXiv:2408.06534) derive Fréchet differentiability through a linearized Monge–Ampère problem with oblique boundary data.
Caja-Lopez, Delgadino, and Kitagawa (arXiv:2605.24232) provide a global divergence-form linear response and quantitative potential stability on uniformly convex domains.
Dong, Lee, and Kim (arXiv:1801.09836) provide relevant conormal and oblique Dini boundary regularity, but not the required tracked causal Hessian-band specialization.
Ponnoprat, Okano, and Imaizumi (arXiv:2307.09257) study one-dimensional transport confidence bands, which do not resolve the multivariate Hessian-margin problem.
